ask: 25% off everything, Friday Nov 27 to Monday Nov 30, on acme.com/sale. Instagram and Facebook.
before: The user first asked for a Black Friday campaign. The one question asked was the offer and when it ends; this is the answer. Nothing else about the sale is known: no code, no stock limit.

arguments.name: Black Friday sale
arguments.theme: 25% off everything at Acme, Friday Nov 27 to Monday Nov 30
arguments.audience: People who follow Acme and buy gifts

steps.why: Offer & Promotion only because a real discount and end date were given. One week, Tue Nov 24 to Mon Nov 30: three days of build-up, then the sale, never past its end. The strategy's own mix has a text post, which Instagram can't take, so the mix is sent without it: images and one carousel both fit Instagram and Facebook.

arguments.context_notes: The offer: 25% off everything at acme.com/sale. It runs Friday Nov 27 to Monday Nov 30 only. Before Nov 27, say it is coming and when; never say it is live. Nothing after Nov 30. No codes, stock limits or countdown claims: none were given.

steps.why: The notes reach the writer word for word every day it writes, so the real offer, dates and limits go here. The strategy already tells it never to invent urgency; the notes add what this sale does not have.
Check before asking to start: starts_on not past, accounts set, resolved_content_mix as sent. Week 1 starts Tue Nov 24, so its drafts are written around Sun Nov 22.

say: Ready, not started: Black Friday sale for Acme, Offer & Promotion (the deal, its price, when it ends). Nov 24 to Nov 30 on Instagram and Facebook: 3 images and 1 carousel, 4 drafts to review, written around Sun Nov 22. Teasers before Friday, the sale Fri to Mon, nothing after. Start it?
never: Inventing a discount, a code, a stock limit or "ends tonight" the user didn't give.
Running an offer campaign past the offer's end date.
A text post in a mix that goes to Instagram.
